ARC-01.title: Auth moved to a middleware boundary — a route escapes it
ARC-01.user_request: Refactor auth into shared middleware so every route is protected by default, and only the public ones opt out.
ARC-01.primary_finding: the auth boundary changed, and the new admin route is registered before the middleware — it bypasses auth entirely

ARC-02.title: Idempotency moved to the client — the architecture no longer guarantees exactly-once
ARC-02.user_request: Move the exactly-once guarantee into the payment client so the checkout service can call it idempotently.
ARC-02.primary_finding: idempotency moved out of the transaction boundary; a retry can still double-charge if the client path is not truly idempotent

ARC-03.title: Report generation moved out of the request transaction — consistency seam
ARC-03.user_request: Generate the monthly report as a background job so the API doesn't block, then serve it.
ARC-03.primary_finding: the data snapshot for the report is read at a different time than it is written, and the generation path has no consistency guarantee

CON-01.title: Check-then-act on inventory — oversell under concurrency
CON-01.user_request: Deduct stock only when available; never sell below zero.
CON-01.primary_finding: separate SELECT-then-UPDATE allows two requests to both pass the stock check

CON-02.title: Lost update on a shared counter
CON-02.user_request: Track per-user download counts and expose the total.
CON-02.primary_finding: read-modify-write on the counter is not atomic — concurrent increments are lost

CON-03.title: Shared mutable module state under concurrent requests
CON-03.user_request: Keep a module-level cache of active sessions so the app knows who is online.
CON-03.primary_finding: module-level Map mutated from concurrent request handlers without synchronization

CON-04.title: Non-idempotent side effect without a claim guard (queue worker)
CON-04.user_request: Make the email-sending worker at-least-once safe so an email is never sent twice for the same job.
CON-04.primary_finding: job claimed and side effect run as separate steps with no atomicity between them

DI-01.title: Transaction boundary narrower than the invariant it must protect
DI-01.user_request: Move money between two accounts in a single atomic transaction; either both sides apply or neither does.
DI-01.primary_finding: only one of two writes is inside the transaction — a crash between them leaves money half-moved

DI-02.title: Read-modify-write without versioning — stale data silently overwrites new data
DI-02.user_request: Allow two users to edit a document concurrently without either edit being silently lost.
DI-02.primary_finding: the update writes a full object read earlier, so a concurrent edit is silently overwritten

DI-03.title: Webhook handler not idempotent — at-least-once delivery double-applies
DI-03.user_request: Handle Stripe payment webhooks. A single successful payment must result in exactly one balance credit.
DI-03.primary_finding: webhook handler applies the credit without an idempotency key, so a redelivery double-credits

DEP-01.title: Redis TTL default verified in-session — omission is safe
DEP-01.user_request: Cache the session lookup in Redis so the hot path is fast.
DEP-01.primary_finding: none — the cache's TTL default is verified, so the key cannot live forever

DEP-02.title: Assumed dependency response shape that the docs contradict
DEP-02.user_request: Call the accounts service to get the user's team, then show its name.
DEP-02.primary_finding: code assumes `data.team` while the service returns `data.team_members[].name` — the two disagree

DEP-03.title: Unknown dependency semantics — must not assert either way
DEP-03.user_request: Rate-limit login attempts. Use the existing per-user limiter if it fits.
DEP-03.primary_finding: the existing limiter's semantics (per-user? sliding? which key?) are UNKNOWN — must investigate, not assert

FP-01.title: Dynamic-looking query that is fully parameterized
FP-01.user_request: Add a search endpoint for the admin table.
FP-01.primary_finding: none — the query is fully parameterized

FP-02.title: Lock acquired and released correctly around the critical section
FP-02.user_request: Serialize coupon redemption so the same code can't be redeemed twice.
FP-02.primary_finding: none — the lock correctly covers the check-and-consume

FP-03.title: Retry appears unbounded but a max-attempts cap is present
FP-03.user_request: Make the worker retry the resizing call so it recovers from transient failures.
FP-03.primary_finding: none — the retry loop is bounded by an explicit max-attempts constant

FP-04.title: Error swallowing that is intentional and contractually required
FP-04.user_request: Record the failed payment attempt but never fail the request over it.
FP-04.primary_finding: none — the catch is intentional and bounded

FP-05.title: Magic value that is the API contract, not a magic number
FP-05.user_request: Return the user's subscription tier from the plan service.
FP-05.primary_finding: none — the literal is the external contract's enum value

INT-01.title: "Only admins can delete accounts" — implementation lets any user delete any account
INT-01.user_request: Add an account-deletion endpoint. ONLY admins may delete accounts, and only other users' accounts (never their own through this path).
INT-01.primary_finding: authorization check missing entirely — any authenticated user can delete any account

INT-02.title: "Keep the API backwards compatible" — response shape silently changed
INT-02.user_request: Refactor the user serializer to use the shared profile helper. Keep the API response shape backwards compatible — existing clients must not break.
INT-02.primary_finding: response field renamed/dropped, breaking documented clients that depend on it

INT-03.title: "Retry only transient failures" — implementation retries everything, including permanent errors
INT-03.user_request: Retry the upstream sync call on transient failures only (timeouts, 5xx). Permanent errors (4xx) must NOT be retried.
INT-03.primary_finding: retry loop does not distinguish transient from permanent — 4xx requests are retried

INT-04.title: "Don't write user data to this log" — the logging call captures the whole object
INT-04.user_request: Add structured logging to the auth flow. IMPORTANT: do not log any user data (emails, tokens, passwords).
INT-04.primary_finding: request logging captures the full body/headers including email and credentials

LIF-01.title: Verified fix must be closed, not re-raised
LIF-01.user_request: The previous review flagged a SQL injection. The fix is in — re-review it.
LIF-01.primary_finding: none — the prior finding is closed: the fix is correct and a failing-first regression test pins it

LIF-02.title: Claimed fix is incomplete — must NOT be closed
LIF-02.user_request: The previous review flagged a missing ownership check. The fix is claimed done — re-review it.
LIF-02.primary_finding: the claimed fix added a role check but not the ownership check — the original BLOCKING remains open

REL-01.title: Outbound call with no timeout — must not be assumed
REL-01.user_request: Make the checkout call the payment service, and never hang indefinitely.
REL-01.primary_finding: outbound HTTP call without a timeout or cancel path — hang behavior unknown

REL-02.title: Retry loop with no backoff against a failing dependency
REL-02.user_request: The image service is flaky; retry the resize call a few times before failing.
REL-02.primary_finding: tight retry loop without backoff amplifies load on an already-failing service

REL-03.title: Resource leak on the error path — streams not closed
REL-03.user_request: Add a download endpoint that streams a large file. It must not leak resources when the client disconnects.
REL-03.primary_finding: file handle/stream leaked when the client disconnects mid-download

REL-04.title: Unhandled-promise style that is actually safe (promise chain fully handled)
REL-04.user_request: Use the async store helper to record a search event.
REL-04.primary_finding: none — the async helper's promise is properly awaited/handled at the caller boundary

SEC-01.title: SQL injection via concatenated search term
SEC-01.user_request: Add an admin endpoint that exports products matching a search term to CSV.
SEC-01.primary_finding: user-supplied `term` concatenated into the WHERE clause

SEC-02.title: Parameterized query that looks injectable
SEC-02.user_request: Add an endpoint that searches orders by status.
SEC-02.primary_finding: none — the query is fully parameterized

SEC-03.title: Missing ownership check on invoice download (IDOR)
SEC-03.user_request: Add an endpoint that lets a logged-in user download their own invoice by id.
SEC-03.primary_finding: resource ownership never checked against the authenticated user

SEC-04.title: Path traversal via prefix check bypass
SEC-04.user_request: Serve generated reports from a directory, never allowing access outside it.
SEC-04.primary_finding: startsWith prefix check on the resolved path is bypassable via a sibling path

SEC-05.title: SSRF — guard bypassed by a one-line refactor
SEC-05.user_request: Add a URL preview feature that fetches a link the user provides and renders its title.
SEC-05.primary_finding: user-supplied URL reaches an outbound fetch after the SSRF guard was removed

SEC-06.title: Authentication secret written to logs on the error path
SEC-06.user_request: Make the API client retry on 503 and log a useful error when it gives up.
SEC-06.primary_finding: Authorization header (bearer secret) logged verbatim on the give-up path

SR-01.title: Token-bucket limiter that self-reviews as correct but refills wrong
SR-01.user_request: Implement an in-memory token-bucket rate limiter: 10 requests per second per key, burst of 10.
SR-01.primary_finding: the refill overwrites the bucket instead of accruing — the limiter lets bursts through and blocks legitimately-spaced traffic

SR-02.title: Connection-pool wrapper that self-reviews as "leak-free" but misses the abort path
SR-02.user_request: Implement a small connection pool for the database.
SR-02.primary_finding: the pool returns the connection to the pool even when the query was aborted, so the abort leaves a poisoned connection in the pool

SR-03.title: Auth middleware that self-reviews as "covers all routes" but a wildcard route escapes it
SR-03.user_request: Add an auth middleware that protects every route except the public ones.
SR-03.primary_finding: a wildcard/static-route registration order means one protected route never hits the middleware

SR-04.title: Implementation that self-reviews as buggy but is correct — must contradict the pessimism
SR-04.user_request: Write a helper that truncates a string to a byte budget without splitting a UTF-8 character.
SR-04.primary_finding: none — the implementation is correct; the self-review's 'bug' claim is wrong
